newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: SQUASH-BAD BOY HILL IN DANGER OF YEAR-LONG BAN.
newsitem.headline: SQUASH-BAD BOY HILL IN DANGER OF YEAR-LONG BAN.

text.p: Australia's bad boy of squash Anthony Hill was in danger of a year-long ban from the professional circuit on Tuesday after an extraordinary ill-tempered display in his match against Pakistan's Zubair Khan at the World Open.

Following an amazing display of petulance during the match, which at one stage saw his opponent writing in agony on the floor after being struck by the ball, defeated Hill vented his anger by hurling his equipment at a wall outside the court and screaming: "It's bloody unbelievable."

Hill, renowned for his bad behaviour on court, was banned for three months by the Professional Squash Association after last year's World Open Championship in Cyprus and banned until the end of the century by Squash Australia after the World Team Championships that followed in Egypt.
John Nimick, the PSA executive director, said he did not see the uproar or the match and would have to await reports before taking any action.
But he added: "After the disciplinary actions earlier, Hill does stand within a few hundred dollars of the fines total that will trigger a year long ban," Nimick said.
Hill was given a conduct warning in the opening game for his argumentative attitude and cautioned later in the match along with Zubair for not pursuing the correct line to the ball.
Zubair eventually won 15-8 10-15 15-4 13-15 15-12 in 59 minutes but only after more stormy scenes when he had reached match point at 14-11 in the fifth game.
The Pakistani collapsed on the floor after apparantly being hit by the ball . While Zubair writhed on the ground, Hill stood quiet in the court.

When, after a three minute break for medical attention, a ball appeared to glance from Zubair's racked during the warm-up and hit the Australian, Hill came screaming out of the court to demand action. "Its a disgrace," he yelled.
"You cannot be allowed to hit your opponent with the ball during a warm-up. He did it deliberately."

Hill continued to rant at tournament officials long after the match was over. While compatriot Craig Rowland was scoring a very creditable win over the sixth seeded Del Harris of England, a finalist last year, Hill was outside the court hurling his equipment at the wall.

Following Rowland's win over Harris, fifth seeded Chris Walker of England beat Zubair's elder brother Zarak Jahan 15-6 15-12 15-11 and Scotland's fourth seeded Peter Nicol survived a spirited attack from Ahmed Barada, Egypt's former world junior champion, to win 12-15 15-2 9-15 15-9 15-13 after trailing 10-13 in the fifth game.
